name: Moldova
snapshot: Maia Sandu's pro-EU government is pushing for membership by 2028, helped by Orbán's fall, while the Russian-backed region of Transnistria rations gas.
culture: Most Moldovans speak Romanian, and many hold Romanian passports. Moldova's wine cellars, including Mileștii Mici with some 200 kilometres of tunnels, are among the world's largest. Folk music, embroidered shirts and hospitality are central. A Russian-speaking minority and the Gagauz, a Turkic Christian people, add diversity.
society: Moldova is one of Europe's poorest countries, and a quarter of its people have emigrated. Transnistria, a breakaway strip with Russian troops, has been outside government control since 1992. Russia-linked networks have been accused of vote-buying in referendums and elections, and Sandu's party won a majority again in 2025.
situation: Moldova, wedged between Romania and Ukraine, is one of Europe's poorest countries and one of its most contested. Russian troops have sat in its breakaway eastern strip, Transnistria, since a 1992 war. President Maia Sandu has set it on course for the EU, and her party held its majority in the September 2025 election against what officials described as a massive Russian vote-buying and disinformation operation. In 2026, the question has been whether Brussels can deliver its side.

Moldova's path is chained to Ukraine's: Hungary's veto on opening negotiating chapters for Ukraine blocked Moldova too. In March 2026 the EU found a workaround, informally opening technical work on the negotiating clusters without the unanimous political vote, and Sandu has named 2028 as a target for accession (Gariwo). Viktor Orbán's defeat in Hungary in April may remove the main obstacle. Meanwhile Russia's energy weapon has backfired on its own client: since Gazprom cut gas in January 2025, Transnistria has rationed gas and suffered blackouts, its economy shrank about 18 percent and industrial output more than 30 percent in 2025, the worst crisis since its founding war (OSW). Chișinău, now powered via Romania, has offered a "convergence fund" for the region, but analysts warn it is unprepared if Transnistria suddenly collapses and has to be absorbed.
power: A parliamentary republic. The prime minister leads the government backed by the 101-seat parliament; the directly elected president shapes foreign policy. Transnistria and the autonomous region of Gagauzia are both strongholds of pro-Russian sentiment.
holders: President Maia Sandu (PAS), since 2020; Prime Minister Vasile Tofan, since July 2026.

update.html: Prime Minister Alexandru Munteanu resigned on 3 July 2026, bringing down his government. Parliament approved investor Vasile Tofan as prime minister on 21 July, and his cabinet has kept EU accession by 2028 as its central goal.
